description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-18) by #1501 round 9, and FIXED in the same
session -- see the DONE section.

PERL: `die` with no arguments, or with an argument that makes the empty
string, does not raise "Died" unconditionally.  perldoc -f die:

  * if `$@` holds a REFERENCE whose class has a PROPAGATE method, the value
    thrown is `$@->PROPAGATE(__FILE__, __LINE__)`;
  * any other reference is re-thrown UNCHANGED;
  * a non-empty string gets `"\t...propagated at FILE line N.\n"` appended;
  * only an EMPTY `$@` gives "Died".

AND `$@` is CLEARED when an eval is ENTERED (perl's CLEAR_ERRSV in
pp_entertry / pp_entereval), so the body -- and anything it calls -- reads ""
and can never see the PREVIOUS eval's error.  The two facts are one: the
reuse rule above is defined in terms of `$@`, and without the entry clear it
reuses whatever error happened to be lying around.

PCL BEFORE: "Died" for all four cases, and `$@` survived into the next eval.

  eval { die "x\n" }; eval { die "" }; print $@;
      perl: Died at F line 1.        PCL: x

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL), the PROPAGATE half:

  package Out; sub PROPAGATE { return bless {}, "Out" }
  eval { die bless {}, "Out" }; eval { die };
  print ref($@), "\n";            # perl: Out   PCL (before): "" ("Died")

  eval { die "Horribly\n" }; eval { die };
  print $@;   # perl: Horribly\n\t...propagated at F line N.\n

=== DONE (s473t6b, Opus, 2026-09-18) â commit 3ac9394f ===

BOTH halves ship together, because the first is DEFINED in terms of $@.

HALF 1 -- the reuse rule, written out for `die` exactly as the runtime has
had it for `warn` all along (`p-warn-build-message` appends "\t...caught at"):
same shape, same predicate (`p-warn-is-reference`), one new helper for the
FILE/LINE split PROPAGATE is handed.

HALF 2 -- the eval ENTRY clear, found by probing what half 1 would BREAK: with
only half 1 in, `eval { die "x\n" }; eval { die "" }` propagated the FIRST
eval's error where perl says "Died".  `p-try` has cleared at entry since #340;
`p-eval-block` and `%p-eval-1` had not.  Probed 5.40.3: the block form, the
string form, and a sub CALLED inside the eval all read "" in perl.

MEASURED
  probes/p2.pl  4 propagate rows wrong -> byte-identical (an `Out` object, an
                ARRAY ref kept with its value, `100\t...propagated at â¦`,
                `Horribly\n\t...propagated at â¦`)
  probes/p8.pl  10 NEGATIVES byte-identical (bare die with an empty $@, a
                plain message, a message with no newline, `die ""`, a LIST, a
                hashref, `die 0`, an argument die after an error, a twice-
                rethrown ref, `die "0"`)
  probes/p9.pl  5 entry-clear rows byte-identical
  companion     op/die.t 5/15 -> 9/11 (`--jobs 1`; 3 blessed rows FIXED)
  companion     op/eval.t 133/35 -> 133/35 â the WIDE half costs NOTHING
  sweep         GATE clean, TOTAL 18686 (+0), 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST
  ir-conform    323 pass, 0 fail, 22 known, 0 stale

GUARD Pl/t/eval-01.t 57 -> 67 rows, three blocks; inverse-verified on a
f26282db extraction: 7 of the 10 FAIL there and the 3 that pass are the
negatives, which is what a negative is for.  ir-spec Â§6.3 gains the entry
clear as step 2 and the reuse rule as a table.


=== REVIEW FIX (Fable, s490, main 158be071) ===
The shipped emptiness test concatenated EVERY die's arguments to ask whether they were empty, so `die $exception_object` ran the class's `""` overload (perl: 0 calls; the batch: 1, and 2 for `die $obj, "x"` where perl runs it once) -- an observable change and a cost on every object die (real exception classes build a trace string there).  Fixed: a list holding a reference is never "empty" and is not stringified to find out; %p-die-reuse-eval-error returns the message it built as a second value so p-die concatenates ONCE.  Given up deliberately: a list whose every overload answers "" (perl would reuse $@).  Guard rows K/L, Pl/t/eval-01.t (67 -> 69).  Probe: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/probes/t6b/p1878.pl + the scratchpad q5 shape embedded in the guard.
subject: die with no arguments must REUSE $@ (PROPAGATE / ref / "...propagated at"), and $@ is cleared on the way INTO an eval
